title: Lixity | Local manuscript analysis and revision
description: See why a 31-word sentence with 22 function words was marked, jump to its paragraph, and compare drafts on your own computer.
eyebrow: 31 words in the sample sentence. 22 are function words.
headline:
See why a sentence is marked.
Read it in the scene.
intro: Click a marked sentence or repeated word to open its paragraph and see every word that was counted. Compare your draft with the last saved version and keep character dossiers and sources beside the manuscript. Analysis runs locally.
demo_note: Edit a passage in the browser sandbox, or open the English demo and try “Check a sticky sentence”.
preview: Lixity showing the opening chapter of The Crate at Warehouse 4 beside the project navigation.
tasks_title: What you can do with Lixity
read_text: Compare your open draft with the saved manuscript. Lixity measures both with the same settings so you can see what changed in the text.
research_title: Check the sequence of a scene
research_text: In Warehouse 4, the first report and its correction put the event in different places. Follow a quotation to the saved source and compare the records on the timeline.
share_text: Export a saved dossier as a PDF with passages and source quotations. For test readers, create a reading website with the chapters and background notes you choose to share.
principle_text: Lixity measures patterns and shows you the passages behind them. Read them in context and decide whether a repetition, a long sentence, or a tense shift fits the scene.
start_text: Choose macOS, Windows or Linux and follow the steps from download to first launch.
scope: The demo shows development version v{version}.
languages_text: The site and app interface are available in seven languages. Choose the manuscript analysis language explicitly; technical documentation remains in English.
limits: Language rules and coverage vary by language, with German and English offering the deepest checks. Switching the interface language never alters your manuscript.
feedback_text: Tell us what you wanted to do and where you got stuck. A few steps or a fictional example are enough.
linguistics_text: Open a mark and read the whole paragraph. See which words or sentences were counted and decide whether the passage needs a change.
language_suggestion: Prefer another language? Use your saved choice or a language supported by your browser.
tour_note: Silent recording of the fictional Warehouse 4 project in the development build.
tour_read: Open a review suggestion and jump to its passage.
tour_passage: See which words counted, why the sentence was marked, and what to check.
tour_compare: Compare the unsaved draft with the manuscript under the same settings.
tour_chapters: Open a chapter measurement and see which chapter it describes.
tour_dossier: Open Mara’s dossier and read her appearances in context.
tour_pdf: Download the saved dossier version as a PDF.
tour_error: The video could not load. Explore the interactive demo instead.
read_alt: Manuscript with a chapter heading, prose and a search bar
linguistics_alt: The highlighted sentence “A board moved.” with its word count and surrounding paragraph.
research_alt: Research workspace with a saved dossier and an action to find dossier suggestions in the manuscript.
share_alt: Revision note on a manuscript paragraph with Save and Cancel actions
answer_marks: Review sentence lengths, recognized quotations and repeated words in a paragraph, then compare chapters. Open a mark to see what was counted.
answer_local: Built-in analysis runs on your computer, where your project files are stored. Optional services such as map providers and external language models have their own data requirements.
question_demo: What can I try before installing?
answer_demo: Edit a paragraph in the browser exercise, which uses simplified rules. The English demo is a larger read-only example project. Install Lixity for full analysis and your own projects.
